# Temple Scroll Column 65 — The LOGOS Bible (Formal)
**Translator:** LOGOS | **Source:** 11Q19 (Cave 11), Col. 65 | **Condition:** well preserved

---

**65:1** The Levitical priests — the entire tribe of Levi — shall have no allotment or inheritance with Israel. They shall subsist on the fire offerings of the LORD and on his portion.

**65:2** They shall have no inheritance among their brothers; the LORD himself is their inheritance, as he promised them.

**65:3** This shall be the rightful due of the priests from the people, from those who offer a sacrifice, whether an ox or a sheep: they shall give the priest the shoulder, the two jowls, and the stomach.

**65:4** The firstfruits of your grain, your new wine, and your oil, and the first yield of the shearing of your flock, you shall give to him.

**65:5** For the LORD your God has chosen him from all your tribes to stand and minister in the name of the LORD — him and his descendants — for all time.

**65:6** If a Levite comes from any of your towns throughout Israel where he has been residing, and comes with wholehearted desire to the place that I shall choose,

**65:7** he may minister in the name of the LORD his God alongside all his fellow Levites who stand in service there before me.

**65:8** They shall eat equal portions, irrespective of what any may have received from the sale of family property.

**65:9** When you enter the land that I am giving you, you shall not learn to imitate the abominable practices of those nations.

**65:10** No one shall be found among you who passes a son or daughter through fire, who practices divination, who reads omens, who interprets signs, or who practices sorcery,

**65:11** or who casts spells, or who consults ghosts or spirits, or who inquires of the dead.

**65:12** For everyone who does these things is abhorrent to the LORD, and it is because of these abominations that the LORD your God is driving them out before you.

**65:13** You shall be wholly devoted to the LORD your God.

**65:14** For these nations you are about to dispossess give heed to those who read omens and practice divination, but the LORD your God has not permitted you to do so.

**65:15** The LORD your God will raise up for you a prophet from among your own people, from your own brothers, a prophet like me; you shall heed him.

**65:16** This accords with what you requested of the LORD your God at Horeb on the day of the assembly, when you said: Let us not hear the voice of the LORD our God again, nor see this great fire any more, or we shall die.

---

*LOGOS notes: Column 65 presents Deut 18:1–16 in the Temple Scroll's characteristic first-person frame. "Jowls" for לחיים is the anatomical term (not "cheeks" which suggests the face). "Wholly devoted" for תמים captures the relational completeness demanded. The prophet-like-Moses passage (65:15) is quoted in Acts 3:22 and 7:37, demonstrating its messianic currency in the Second Temple period. The scroll preserves "Horeb" (the Deuteronomic name for Sinai).*
